title: Discover linked repos: relai index build --scan <folder> and relai discover --links <folder>
description: Product goal (owner, 2026-11-04): drive several LINKED repos from one central place, for teams. Today nothing finds the repos or their links by itself: the index needs a hand-written list, provides/consumes are declared by hand, a repo without relai init is invisible to find and workspace. Needed: (1) index build --scan <folder>: find git repos, report which have relai.yaml / tracker / AGENTS.md, no list file. (2) discover --links <folder>: graph of MENTIONS between sibling repos (names in docs, compose files, remote URLs, submodules, dependencies) with counts; proposes relai.yaml provides/consumes for a person or agent to confirm, never declares a link by itself (a mention is not a verified link). Decision gate: build it if the test session confirms the gap (it is expected to). Test data: the HOMELAB cluster (HOMELAB cites portfolio, Shelfmark, patrimoine, freelance, rudy-ops, COACH, navidrome...).
notes:
Implemented on feat/discover-links (OpenSpec discover-linked-repos). Not yet measured with an agent following --prompt, nor on precision of strong/weak beyond the owner's own folder.

title: relai new copies the content of symbolic links (secret file leak) and leaves a half-filled destination on error
description:
Source: test report, RELAI M3. Reproduced 2026-11-04: a template containing `creds -> /path/outside.txt` yields a regular file with the target's content in the new repo. With a template cloned by URL, a third-party template can embed a secret file of the machine that instantiates it. A symlink to a directory or a broken symlink makes the copy fail with a half-filled destination, and the retry is refused (non-empty).

Cause: internal/scaffold/scaffold.go, `Copy` uses `os.ReadFile`, which follows links.

Fix: `Lstat` / `d.Type()`; either refuse symlinks with a clear message or recreate them only when the target stays inside the template; never read through them. On any error, remove the destination that this run created.

Acceptance: tests for file symlink, dir symlink, broken symlink, link escaping the template; destination absent after a failure.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the independent light test of 2026-11-04 exercised only some of these (handoff speed, bd cache, symlinks in relai new, flags after arguments, installer without sudo, find on tricky manifests). close_reason: Fixed, tested and merged (PRs #8, #9, #10, 2026-11-04); confirmed by the independent light test of 2026-11-04 where it was in scope.

title: relai find misses provides/consumes that are not in block syntax (inline, scalar, comments, multi-key)
description:
Source: test report 2026-11-03, RELAI M2. Reproduced 2026-11-04 on 4 repos: only the block form `- capability: x` is found; `provides: [{capability: x}]` (the syntax written in the cross-repo-index spec scenario itself), scalar items `- x`, a comment line inside the list, and a two-key item where `capability:` is not first are all dropped silently. `relai find` then says nothing provides X and the user builds a duplicate, the opposite of the product goal. The tester's 300 generated repos (inline syntax) gave 0 capabilities.

Cause: internal/index/index.go, `parseManifest` / `blockList` (stops at blank or comment lines, only reads `capability:` as first key, no flow syntax).

Fix: accept flow lists of scalars or maps, scalar block items, comments and blank lines inside a list, and `capability:` in any key position. Warn (to stderr, in `index build`) whenever a `provides:`/`consumes:` key yields nothing or a value is not understood. Decide whether to move to a real YAML parser: the 2026-11-03 decision was a hand-rolled subset, which is fine only if the subset is documented and unknown shapes are reported.

Acceptance: table test with each form above giving the same result; spec scenario `provides: [{capability: x}]` passes as written; warning test for an unparsable value.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the independent light test of 2026-11-04 exercised only some of these (handoff speed, bd cache, symlinks in relai new, flags after arguments, installer without sudo, find on tricky manifests). The others are covered by unit tests only, not by an independent test. Discovery (relai-fwx) was not in that test.

title: Degraded-mode handoff takes 9 s to 150 s on a large repo (quadratic trimming)
description:
Source: test report, RELAI M1 and minor m1. Synthetic repo with 10,000 commits and 5,000 touched files: 9.4-12.5 s, versus 0.40 s with `--max-tokens 1000000`. With 20,000 touched files and 20,000 TODO markers: 150.6 s. A SessionStart hook blocked for minutes is unacceptable.

Cause: internal/handoff/handoff.go:53-81, `Build` re-renders the whole document for every item removed (O(n^2)). The notes trimming loop (handoff.go:73-77) has the same shape: notes.md of 5,000 lines = 2.4 s, 10,000 = 10.4 s, 20,000 = 47 s, 100,000 lines = over 120 s.

Fix: compute how many items fit in one pass (estimate per-item token cost once, cut, then re-check once), or binary search. Cap the inputs early (read only the last N lines of notes, only the first K touched files).

Acceptance: benchmark test with the 10,000/5,000 fixture under 1 s and the 100,000-line notes under 1 s; output identical for small inputs (determinism tests unchanged).
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the independent light test of 2026-11-04 exercised only some of these (handoff speed, bd cache, symlinks in relai new, flags after arguments, installer without sudo, find on tricky manifests). title: Flags placed after the positional argument are silently ignored (init --no-claude, index build -o, find --index)
description:
Source: test report, RELAI M4. Reproduced 2026-11-04: `relai init z2 --no-claude` still creates `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md`; `relai index build repos.txt -o idx.json` writes `.relai/index.json`; `relai find auth.oidc --index x.json` ignores `--index`. Go's `flag` stops at the first positional argument. Already noted in .relai/notes.md as a pitfall, never fixed. The most invasive action runs while the user thinks they opted out.

Fix: a small helper used by every subcommand that reorders args (flags first) or errors out on a flag-looking token after a positional (`flag provided after argument: --no-claude, put it before`). Prefer reordering, and cover every subcommand.

Acceptance: a table test over all subcommands with flags before and after the positional, same result.
notes: CORRECTION to the close reason: the independent light test of 2026-11-04 exercised only some of these (handoff speed, bd cache, symlinks in relai new, flags after arguments, installer without sudo, find on tricky manifests). The others are covered by unit tests only, not by an independent test. Discovery (relai-fwx) was not in that test.
